s2.p1: Laos has **no WDSF member** federation. A Lao DanceSports Federation (LADSF) was set up only recently, and years of advocacy won it a National Games spot.
s2.p2: Partner dancing lives in salsa and bachata classes, like those at ==Fanglao Dance Studio== in Vientiane. The national dance is the **lamvong**.

s3.p: Lamvong dancers count from **one to eight**, again and again, for the whole song. The count sets where the feet and hands go.

s4.p1: **Phetnilan “Golf” Keovongsy** won the Lao HipHop Festival 2024, then went to Kaohsiung, Taiwan, as Laos’s only competitor.
s4.p2: He finished ==third== in the solo battle. In 2024 he trained at **That Luang**, 6 to 9 pm, and invited anyone to join.

s5.name: LAMVONG
s5.p: Born as a **rice-harvest** dance around a bale of rice. Men circle inside, women outside, counterclockwise. It is an essential part of every wedding party.

s5.name: LAO RAMAYANA
s5.p: **Phra Lak Phra Lam**, the Lao Ramayana, came with Buddhist missions centuries ago. Royal dancers once performed it for the king.

s6.p: After the **1975 revolution**, the royal dance-drama fell out of favour for years. Revived from the 1990s, it got its own Luang Prabang theatre in 2003.

s7.p: Inscribed as Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity on **5 December**. On New Year’s Eve, **thousands** joined a lamvong tribute at Patuxay Park, Vientiane.
s7.p2: In 2025, DanceSport was approved as a **National Games** medal sport for the first time, with breaking, couple and team events.
